2026-12-04.title: Friday of the First Week of Advent
readings: On that day the eyes of the blind shall see
The Lord is my light and my salvation
Two blind men believe in Jesus and are healed
2026-12-04.alt: First Friday of the month. Optional memorial: St John Damascene, priest and doctor.
2026-12-04.verse: Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”
theo: Isaiah describes the transformation God will bring: Lebanon becomes a fruitful field, “the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see”, the meek find joy, the tyrant disappears. Advent is the season of this hope.

Two blind men follow Jesus crying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!” They call him by his messianic title, though they cannot see him. In the house Jesus asks them one question: “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” “Yes, Lord.” He touches their eyes: “According to your faith let it be done to you.” Their eyes are opened. Faith sees before the eyes do. St John Damascene, remembered today, defended the veneration of icons: in Christ the invisible God has become visible, and we may look on his face.
outline: Ask: what are you unable to see in your life right now?
Jesus asks for faith before he heals.
Point 3 · The Lord is my light
“According to your faith let it be done to you.”
live: Tell Jesus in prayer: “Yes, Lord, I believe you can do this,” naming your need.
Go to Confession or spend time before the Blessed Sacrament.
2026-12-04.prayer: Son of David, have mercy on me. Touch the eyes of my heart, increase my faith, and be my light and my salvation this Advent. Amen.
altar: At every Mass we pray: Lord, have mercy. It is the cry of the blind men, and the Heart of Jesus answers it in the Eucharist.

quick: God promises that the blind will see.
Jesus asks: Do you believe I can do this?
Faith sees before the eyes do.
2026-12-04.action: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday.
2026-12-04.question: Do I really believe Jesus can change my situation?

family.explain: Two blind men asked Jesus for mercy, and because they believed, he healed them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind or sick, and for anyone who cannot see God's love.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we believe Jesus can help us? What shall we ask him for?”

pm.open: Sacred Heart of Jesus, on this First Friday we cry with the blind men: Son of David, have mercy on us. Open our eyes to your love. Amen.
share: Jesus asks: do you believe that I am able to do this? (Matthew 9:28). What do I find hard to believe Jesus can do?
What is my blindness: to God, to others, or to myself?
How will I honour the Sacred Heart this First Friday?
pm.resp: Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of the Heart of Jesus.
For the blind, the deaf and all with disabilities, that they may be respected and helped.
For those spiritually blind, that their eyes may be opened.
For sinners, that they may find mercy in confession this Advent.
For our families, that we may see one another's needs.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you opened the eyes of the blind. Touch our hearts and our eyes, and let it be done to us according to our faith. Amen.

illus: A businessman in Thrissur said he had never noticed the beggar outside his office for ten years. One First Friday, after confession, he stopped, talked with the man and learnt his name. “I was the blind one,” he said.

homily: Dear friends, on this First Friday of December Isaiah promises a reversal: in a very little while Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field. On that day the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see (Isaiah 29:17–18). The meek shall obtain fresh joy in the Lord.

In the Gospel two blind men follow Jesus, crying out: have mercy on us, Son of David! It is a cry of faith; they call him by his messianic title. Jesus asks them: do you believe that I am able to do this? They say: yes, Lord. He touches their eyes and says: according to your faith let it be done to you (Matthew 9:27–29).
Jesus asks the same question of each of us this Advent: do you believe that I am able to do this? Able to heal your blindness, to change your heart, to restore your family, to forgive your sin?
There is a blindness worse than physical blindness: not seeing God's love, not seeing the needs of others, not seeing our own sins. The two blind men knew they were blind. Many of us do not.
On the First Friday we honour the Sacred Heart of Jesus. From that Heart flows the mercy the blind men begged for. The simplest prayer of the Church, Lord, have mercy, is their prayer.

Today, let us make their prayer ours. Let us name one blindness in our life and ask Jesus to touch it. If possible, let us go to confession and receive Holy Communion in honour of the Sacred Heart. And let us answer his question with faith: yes, Lord, I believe. Amen.
kids: Children, two blind men asked Jesus for help and He opened their eyes. When you pray, believe that Jesus can help you!

intro: God promises sight; Jesus asks for faith; faith sees in the dark.

sub: The deaf hear, the blind see.
q: On that day the deaf shall hear the words of a scroll, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.
Then he shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
points.apply: Pray for someone who cannot see God's hand in their life.

sub: The blind men followed and cried out.
q: Those of steadfast mind you keep in peace—in peace because they trust in you.

When he entered the house, the blind men came to him; and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.” Then he touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith let it be done to you.”
points.apply: Say “Yes, Lord, I believe” about your deepest need.

sub: The invisible God became visible in Christ.
We look on his face in prayer.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son, full of grace and truth.
points.apply: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament today.

concl: Christ is our light this Advent.
2026-12-04.resolve: Make a holy hour this First Friday or next week.
